constraints.quote: * decided: Rust and Swift share one line reader because both write docs as `///` lines, nest by braces, and need the same header, tag and hash steps

must_name.grading: Name the listed constraints and the minimum affected-symbol subset; extra correctly justified symbols are allowed.

source.why: The shared pass is readLines, and Rust and Swift call it directly as their extraction result (src/line-reader.pure.ts:155; src/extract-rust.pure.ts:102; src/extract-swift.pure.ts:83). Kotlin also calls it before applying Kotlin-specific deduplication and module-name work, so the header mentioning only Rust and Swift is not a complete current caller inventory (src/extract-kotlin.pure.ts:117).
source.ambiguity: New language-specific function names are implementation choices and are not part of the expected list; scanBraces and declarationEnd can remain shared because the request explicitly preserves low-level scanners. Merely renaming readLines or adding wrappers that still use its shared pass does not meet the requested reversal.
source.constraint_on_other_symbol_or_file: The file-header decision covers three language readers in other files; Kotlin is a caller not named in that decision text.
